# Calum Lill: A Comprehensive Biographical and Critical Report
## Executive Summary
Calum Lill (born 1995 or 1996\) is a British actor who has established himself as a significant figure in contemporary television drama, most notably through his defining role as the villainous solicitor Joel Deering in the long-running ITV soap opera *Coronation Street*.1 His trajectory from a working-class background in the north of England to a central antagonist in one of the UK's most culturally significant broadcasts represents a compelling narrative of resilience within the performing arts industry.

Lill's career is characterized by a distinct dichotomy: the ability to portray psychologically complex, manipulative antagonists on screen, juxtaposed with a career in pantomime and comedic stage work . His portrayal of Joel Deering (2023–2024) anchored a major grooming storyline and a high-profile murder mystery, earning him critical acclaim and nominations at the Inside Soap Awards and the British Soap Awards . Beyond his television work, Lill has demonstrated versatility through his involvement in independent film, specifically the feature *Derelict*, and his return to the stage in the critically lauded thriller *The Sociable Plover* in 2025 .

As of December 17, 2025, Lill has successfully transitioned from his soap opera tenure into a diverse portfolio of stage and screen work, while also managing a secondary career as an acting coach through his company, Screen Ready . This report provides an exhaustive analysis of his life, career, artistic techniques, and public reception.

## Early Life and Educational Background
### Formative Years and Influences
Born in **1995 or 1996**, Calum Lill was raised in a working-class family in the United Kingdom . His early connection to the television industry was serendipitous and deeply personal. Lill has cited the BBC school-based drama *Waterloo Road* as his favorite television programme during his childhood . In a coincidence that would foreshadow his future career, Lill revealed that his childhood home was utilized as a filming location for *Waterloo Road* during the show's early production years . This occurred just as his family was vacating the property, establishing a tangible link between his domestic life and the world of television production. He has stated that his primary ambition as a youth was to secure an acting role on that specific series, highlighting an early fixation on the medium of television drama .

### Professional Training
Lill pursued formal vocational training at the **Arts Educational Schools (ArtsEd)** in London, one of the UK's premier drama schools . He graduated in **2018** with a BA Hons in Acting . His training at ArtsEd was comprehensive, equipping him with a skillset that extended beyond classical acting techniques.

His casting profile indicates specialized training in physical disciplines that would later prove essential for his roles in action-heavy soap opera storylines. Specifically, Lill possesses training in:

* **Stage Combat and Weaponry:** Listed skills include "Weapons Training" and "Military Tactics (Close Quarters)" . This background suggests a proficiency in choreography and safety required for the violent confrontations he would later enact as Joel Deering. 
* **Martial Arts:** He is trained in boxing, a skill that contributes to the physicality and aggressive posturing required for villainous roles . 
* **Sports:** He is a skilled skier, indicating a high level of general athleticism .

This rigorous training provided the technical foundation for his ability to sustain the physical and emotional demands of serial drama production.

## The "Grind" and Career Struggles (2018–2022)
### The Reality of the Industry
Following his graduation in 2018, Lill entered a highly competitive marketplace. While he secured initial guest roles, his career trajectory was not immediately linear. The period between 2018 and 2023 was marked by the instability characteristic of the acting profession, exacerbated by the global COVID-19 pandemic which decimated production schedules across the UK .

Lill has been vocal about the financial and psychological toll of this period. To support himself and save for a house with his partner, he worked a variety of non-acting jobs . One notable position was working on a paella stall at festivals . Interestingly, this job was operated by former *Coronation Street* actors **Jenny Platt** (who played Violet Wilson) and **Rupert Hill** (who played Jamie Baldwin). This connection placed him in the orbit of the show long before he was cast, with the veteran actors providing him with encouragement during his auditions .

### The Car Salesman Era
The most significant period of struggle occurred immediately prior to his breakthrough. Lill worked as a car salesman, a job he has candidly described as detesting . In interviews with *Digital Spy* and the *Manchester Evening News*, Lill revealed that he had reached a breaking point. After nearly 15 years of pursuing acting (including his youth and training), he felt that "nothing was happening" and seriously considered abandoning the profession .

"I was selling cars while auditioning for Corrie and I hated it. I thought: 'It's been 15 years, I'm going to have to drop it, nothing's happening'." — Calum Lill 11

This narrative of the "struggling actor" became a key part of his public persona, resonating with fans and aspiring actors alike. He described the moment he received the call for *Coronation Street* as a cinematic turning point. Standing on the forecourt between two cars, he received a call from his agent. After a tense silence, he was told, "You got it." Lill described his reaction as falling to his knees and "sobbing," overwhelmed by the validation of his persistence .

## Early Television Career
Before his major breakthrough, Lill built his résumé through the traditional route of guest appearances in British medical dramas and soaps. These roles, while brief, demonstrated his range and ability to integrate into established ensembles.

### *Doctors*** **(2019)
Lill's television debut occurred in the BBC One daytime soap *Doctors*. He appeared in **Series 20, Episode 65**, titled "Division," which first broadcast on **February 15, 2019**.13

* **Role:** Chez Wilson-Needham . 
* **Significance:** This was credited as a "Lead Guest Role" . In the format of *Doctors*, the "Story of the Day" often revolves entirely around the guest characters, placing a significant burden of narrative carriage on the visiting actor. Lill remarked humorously on this experience, noting that despite the shoot lasting only two days, he felt as though he had been cast as "the lead in the new Scorsese epic," highlighting his enthusiasm and the weight he placed on this early opportunity .

### *Holby City*** **(2019)
Later in 2019, Lill appeared in the BBC prime-time medical drama *Holby City*.

* **Episode:** Series 21, Episode 41, titled "This Be The Verse" . 
* **Broadcast Date:** October 8, 2019 . 
* **Role:** Conor Henson . 
* **Context:** He appeared alongside series stalwarts like Hugh Quarshie (Ric Griffin). Lill described the experience of working on the *Holby* set as "fantastic," further cementing his comfort in high-pressure television environments .

### *Hollyoaks*** **(2021)
Lill's first recurring role came in the Channel 4 soap *Hollyoaks*, known for its younger demographic and stylized storytelling.

* **Role:** P.C. Carlton Smith . 
* **Tenure:** March to July 2021 (12 episodes) . 
* **Narrative Function:** P.C. Smith was introduced as a colleague and friend of the character **George Kiss**, a corrupt and abusive police officer. The storyline centered on the investigation into George's death ("Who Killed George?"). Lill’s character served as a narrative antagonist to the McQueen family and a symbol of the police force's closing ranks. 
* **Key Episodes:** His appearances included Episode 5629 (July 8, 2021\) and Episode 5630 (July 9, 2021), where his character interacted with Sally St. Claire during the climax of the investigation . 
* **Performance:** This role allowed Lill to practice the authoritative, procedural physicality he would later refine as a solicitor in *Coronation Street*, although P.C. Smith was a more functional, less psychologically explored character than Joel Deering.

## *Coronation Street*****: The Joel Deering Era (2023–2025)
Lill's casting as **Joel Deering** in ITV's *Coronation Street* was the defining moment of his career to date. The role required a commitment of over a year and demanded a complex, bifurcated performance.

### Casting and Character Introduction
Lill made his first on-screen appearance in **Episode 11,054**, aired on **September 7, 2023**.18 Joel Deering was introduced as a duty solicitor—a professional, articulate, and seemingly kind-hearted individual.

* **Strategic Deception:** The show's producers and writers, led by Iain MacLeod, deliberately positioned Joel as a "nice guy" to disarm the audience . He was paired romantically with **Dee-Dee Bailey** (Channique Sterling-Brown), a beloved character known for her moral compass and intelligence. 
* **Chemistry:** Lill and Sterling-Brown developed a strong on-screen rapport, making the couple a fan favorite. This emotional investment from the audience was a calculated narrative tactic to maximize the impact of the eventual betrayal .

### The Grooming Storyline: A Study in Manipulation
The defining arc of Lill's tenure was the revelation that Joel was the predator behind the disappearance of teenager **Lauren Bolton** (Cait Fitton).

* **The Turn:** The narrative shifted from a romance to a psychological thriller. Under his polished exterior, Joel was revealed to groom, manipulate, and abuse vulnerable young women . 
* **Performance Nuance:** Lill was praised for his ability to switch modes. In public scenes with the Bailey family, he maintained a facade of warmth and professional competence. In private scenes with Lauren, he utilized the physical intimidation and cold detachment of an abuser. Lill described this as a challenge of "playing him nice, playing him funny, playing him boring, playing him horrific" . 
* **Violence and Control:** The storyline culminated in the revelation that Joel had beaten Lauren viciously with a chair leg, leaving her for dead—a crime for which the innocent Roy Cropper had been wrongly imprisoned . The brutality of the act, contrasted with Joel's clean-cut image, served as a commentary on the invisibility of violence committed by professional, middle-class men.

### The "Whodunnit" Mystery (Late 2024\)
Lill's exit from the show was structured as a classic "Whodunnit" mystery, a staple of the soap opera genre used to generate high viewer engagement.

* **The Disappearance:** In September 2024, as the legal net tightened, Joel failed to appear in court. His car was found abandoned near a bridge with a suicide note, leading police to initially suspect suicide . 
* **The Murder Investigation:** The discovery of Joel's body in a river changed the inquiry to murder. Post-mortem evidence proved he was dead before entering the water, killed by a blow from a heavy weapon . 
* **The Suspects:** The writers cast suspicion on a wide range of characters, creating a "Cluedo" scenario for the audience. Suspects included: 
 * **Dee-Dee Bailey:** The scorned fiancée. 
 * **Ronnie and Ed Bailey:** Dee-Dee's protective family members who were seen with a crowbar . 
 * **DS Lisa Swain:** The detective obsessed with catching him. 
 * **Mason Radcliffe:** A local troublemaker. 
 * **Kit Green:** A corrupt police officer .

### The Reveal and Exit (November 2024\)
The mystery was resolved in a stylized flashback episode broadcast on **November 15, 2024**.3

* **The Sequence of Events:** The episode revealed that Joel had a chaotic final night (September 27, 2024). He was confronted and attacked by Ronnie and Ed, threatened by Kit, pushed by Max Turner, and verbally eviscerated by Dee-Dee . 
* **The Killer:** Ultimately, it was revealed that **Lauren Bolton**, his victim, struck the fatal blow in self-defense during a confrontation on a railway embankment . 
* **Lill's Analysis:** Lill publicly endorsed this conclusion as "soap justice." He argued that it was thematically appropriate for Joel to be brought down by the very person he had underestimated and victimized .

### 2025 Return
Despite his character's death, Lill made a brief return to the set in **2025**. He appeared in **Episode 11,604** (June 23, 2025\) as a hallucination . This cameo allowed the show to explore the lingering psychological trauma of his victims, proving that the character's shadow remained over Weatherfield long after his physical demise.

## Critical Reception and Cultural Impact
Lill's performance as Joel Deering resonated deeply with audiences and critics, elevating him from a working actor to a recognizable soap star.

### Industry Awards and Nominations
Lill's work was recognized by the two primary award bodies in the British soap industry.

| Year | Award Body | Category | Result | Ref. |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **2024** | **Inside Soap Awards** | Best Villain | Shortlisted | 4 |
| **2024** | **Inside Soap Awards** | Best Showstopper (Joel's Secret) | Shortlisted | 4 |
| **2025** | **British Soap Awards** | Villain of the Year | Nominated | 5 |

Note: While he was a strong contender, the "Villain of the Year" award at the 2025 British Soap Awards was won by Navin Chowdhry for his role as Nish Panesar in EastEnders .

### "Nan Sue" and Viral Fame
A unique aspect of Lill's public reception was the involvement of his grandmother, affectionately known as "Nan Sue." Lill utilized TikTok and Instagram to share videos of his grandmother reacting to his on-screen villainy.

* **The Phenomenon:** In a viral clip watched over 8 million times, Nan Sue was recorded watching the episode where Joel is revealed as the attacker. Her genuine shock and admonishment of her grandson—"You mean to tell me my grandson's a killer? You battered her\!"—became a sensation . 
* **Impact:** This content served a crucial public relations function. It humanized Lill, distinguishing the charming actor from the loathsome character, and provided a comedic counter-narrative to the dark storylines he was enacting. Lill noted that she would text him after episodes saying, "You were really bad, that's a compliment" .

### Critical Assessment
Reviews of his tenure highlighted his ability to embody the "banality of evil." By playing Joel not as a caricature but as a professional, integrated member of society, Lill made the character's crimes more unsettling. *Digital Spy* noted the effectiveness of the "whodunnit" conclusion, while *The Manchester Evening News* praised his handling of the "Whodunnit" flashback sequences .

## Theatre and Film Career (2024–2025)
Following his exit from *Coronation Street*, Lill demonstrated a strategic versatility, moving immediately into stage roles that contrasted sharply with his soap persona.

### Pantomime: The Villain Tradition
Leveraging his profile as a "soap baddie," Lill became a headline attraction in the British pantomime circuit.

* **2024 Season:** He played **Fleshcreep** in *Jack and the Beanstalk* at the Bournemouth Pavilion . 
* **2025 Season:** He was cast to reprise the role of **Fleshcreep** in *Jack and the Beanstalk* at the **Oak Theatre** in Southport, running from December 13 to December 24, 2025 . 
* **Performance Style:** Reviews for his pantomime performances noted his ability to engage with audiences, bringing a playful menace that capitalized on his TV notoriety while adhering to the family-friendly format of the genre .

### Serious Drama: *The Sociable Plover*
In a move to re-establish his credentials as a serious dramatic actor, Lill starred in a revival of **Tim Whitnall**'s play *The Sociable Plover*.

* **Production:** The play ran at the **Old Red Lion Theatre** in Islington, London, from **May 13 to May 24, 2025**.7 
* **Format:** A tense "two-hander" thriller/black comedy. 
* **Role:** Lill played **Dave**, acting opposite **Jack Robertson**.28 
* **Reception:** The production was critically acclaimed for its pacing and "Hitchcockian" atmosphere. 
* **Awards:** Lill and Robertson were jointly awarded the **Standing Ovation Award** for "Best Duo Performance" (Two-Hander) at the **2025 London Pub Theatres Awards**.29 This award validated Lill's ability to hold a stage in an intimate, high-stakes dramatic environment, separating him from the ensemble nature of soap opera work.

### Feature Film: *Derelict*
Lill also ventured into independent film, securing a role in the feature film ***Derelict***.2

* **Context:** While details on the film's wide release are less prominent than his TV work, his involvement in a full-length feature demonstrates his ambition to diversify his portfolio beyond television. The film is described as a thriller, aligning with the darker tone of his recent work.

## Business Ventures: Screen Ready
Beyond his performance work, Lill has established himself as an educator in the field of acting. He operates a coaching company titled **Screen Ready**.2

* **Mission:** The company focuses on helping other actors navigate the industry, likely drawing on his own experiences of resilience and the transition from drama school to professional sets. 
* **Significance:** This venture indicates a commitment to the craft and a desire to mentor the next generation of talent, potentially serving as a secondary income stream that provides stability against the fluctuations of acting work.

## Personal Life
Calum Lill currently resides in **Manchester**, a strategic base for actors working in northern-produced television (such as *Coronation Street* and *Hollyoaks*) .

### Relationship and Family
Lill has been in a long-term relationship with **Roberta McClarron** since **2021**.1 He has frequently credited McClarron as a stabilizing force in his life, particularly during the difficult years prior to his *Coronation Street* casting. He noted that she witnessed his depression while working as a car salesman and supported him through his financial struggles .

Engagement: 
The couple became engaged in June 2024\. Lill revealed in interviews that he had hidden the engagement ring in his dressing room at the Coronation Street studios to keep it secret from McClarron before the proposal . He announced the news on Instagram with a photo of the ring and the caption, "About time I made an honest woman of her" . 
Fatherhood: 
In December 2025, Lill announced that he and McClarron were expecting their first child. The announcement was made via a festive social media post featuring McClarron's baby bump painted as a snowman. Lill captioned the image "New character dropping April '26," confirming the due date for the following spring .

## Conclusion
As of late 2025, Calum Lill occupies a prominent position in the British entertainment landscape. His career serves as a case study in the modern path of a British character actor: rigorous training at a top drama school, a period of significant professional struggle ("the grind"), a breakthrough in a legacy soap opera, and a subsequent diversification into stage and film.

His portrayal of Joel Deering stands as his most significant cultural contribution to date, providing *Coronation Street* with one of its most complex villains of the 2020s. However, his immediate transition into award-winning theatre (*The Sociable Plover*) and his ongoing work in film suggest an actor intent on avoiding typecasting. With a growing family and a diverse portfolio of work across comedy, thriller, and drama genres, Lill has successfully navigated the perilous transition from "soap star" to established working actor.

Calum Lill appeared in *Coronation Street* Episode 11,604 (June 23, 2025) as a hallucination.
Calum Lill's cameo allowed *Coronation Street* to explore the lingering psychological trauma of Joel's victims.
Calum Lill's character's shadow remained over Weatherfield long after his physical demise.
Calum Lill's performance as Joel Deering resonated deeply with audiences and critics, elevating him from a working actor to a recognizable soap star.
Calum Lill was shortlisted for Best Villain at the 2024 Inside Soap Awards.
Calum Lill was shortlisted for Best Showstopper (Joel's Secret) at the 2024 Inside Soap Awards.
Calum Lill was nominated for Villain of the Year at the 2025 British Soap Awards.
The "Villain of the Year" award at the 2025 British Soap Awards was won by Navin Chowdhry for his role as Nish Panesar in EastEnders.
A unique aspect of Calum Lill's public reception was the involvement of his grandmother, affectionately known as "Nan Sue."
Calum Lill utilized TikTok and Instagram to share videos of his grandmother reacting to his on-screen villainy.
In a viral clip watched over 8 million times, Nan Sue was recorded watching the episode where Joel is revealed as the attacker.
Nan Sue's genuine shock and admonishment of her grandson—"You mean to tell me my grandson's a killer? You battered her!"—became a sensation.
The content featuring Nan Sue served a crucial public relations function.
The content featuring Nan Sue humanized Calum Lill, distinguishing the charming actor from the loathsome character.
The content featuring Nan Sue provided a comedic counter-narrative to the dark storylines Calum Lill was enacting.
Calum Lill noted that Nan Sue would text him after episodes saying, "You were really bad, that's a compliment".
Reviews of Calum Lill's tenure highlighted his ability to embody the "banality of evil".
By playing Joel not as a caricature but as a professional, integrated member of society, Calum Lill made the character's crimes more unsettling.
*Digital Spy* noted the effectiveness of the "whodunnit" conclusion for Joel's storyline.
*The Manchester Evening News* praised Calum Lill's handling of the "Whodunnit" flashback sequences.
Leveraging his profile as a "soap baddie," Calum Lill became a headline attraction in the British pantomime circuit.
In the 2024 season, Calum Lill played Fleshcreep in *Jack and the Beanstalk* at the Bournemouth Pavilion.
In the 2025 season, Calum Lill was cast to reprise the role of Fleshcreep in *Jack and the Beanstalk* at the Oak Theatre in Southport.
The pantomime *Jack and the Beanstalk* at the Oak Theatre in Southport was running from December 13 to December 24, 2025.

Reviews for Calum Lill's pantomime performances noted his ability to engage with audiences, bringing a playful menace that capitalized on his TV notoriety while adhering to the family-friendly format of the genre.
Calum Lill starred in a revival of Tim Whitnall's play *The Sociable Plover*.
*The Sociable Plover* ran at the Old Red Lion Theatre in Islington, London, from May 13 to May 24, 2025.
*The Sociable Plover* is a tense "two-hander" thriller/black comedy.
Calum Lill played Dave in *The Sociable Plover*, acting opposite Jack Robertson.
The production of *The Sociable Plover* was critically acclaimed for its pacing and "Hitchcockian" atmosphere.
Calum Lill and Jack Robertson were jointly awarded the Standing Ovation Award for "Best Duo Performance" (Two-Hander) at the 2025 London Pub Theatres Awards.
The Standing Ovation Award validated Calum Lill's ability to hold a stage in an intimate, high-stakes dramatic environment, separating him from the ensemble nature of soap opera work.
Calum Lill ventured into independent film, securing a role in the feature film *Derelict*.
Calum Lill's involvement in a full-length feature film demonstrates his ambition to diversify his portfolio beyond television.
The film *Derelict* is described as a thriller.
Calum Lill has established himself as an educator in the field of acting.
Calum Lill operates a coaching company titled Screen Ready.
Screen Ready focuses on helping other actors navigate the industry.
The Screen Ready venture indicates Calum Lill's commitment to the craft and a desire to mentor the next generation of talent.
The Screen Ready venture potentially serves as a secondary income stream that provides stability against the fluctuations of acting work.
Calum Lill currently resides in Manchester.
Manchester is a strategic base for actors working in northern-produced television (such as *Coronation Street* and *Hollyoaks*).
Calum Lill has been in a long-term relationship with Roberta McClarron since 2021.
Calum Lill has frequently credited Roberta McClarron as a stabilizing force in his life, particularly during the difficult years prior to his *Coronation Street* casting.
Calum Lill noted that Roberta McClarron witnessed his depression while working as a car salesman and supported him through his financial struggles.
Calum Lill and Roberta McClarron became engaged in June 2024.
Calum Lill revealed in interviews that he had hidden the engagement ring in his dressing room at the Coronation Street studios to keep it secret from McClarron before the proposal.
Calum Lill announced his engagement news on Instagram with a photo of the ring and the caption, "About time I made an honest woman of her".
In December 2025, Calum Lill announced that he and Roberta McClarron were expecting their first child.
The announcement of Calum Lill and Roberta McClarron expecting their first child was made via a festive social media post featuring McClarron's baby bump painted as a snowman.
Calum Lill captioned the image "New character dropping April '26," confirming the due date for the following spring.
As of late 2025, Calum Lill occupies a prominent position in the British entertainment landscape.

Calum Lill's career serves as a case study in the modern path of a British character actor: rigorous training at a top drama school, a period of significant professional struggle ("the grind"), a breakthrough in a legacy soap opera, and a subsequent diversification into stage and film.
Calum Lill's portrayal of Joel Deering stands as his most significant cultural contribution to date, providing *Coronation Street* with one of its most complex villains of the 2020s.
Calum Lill's immediate transition into award-winning theatre (*The Sociable Plover*) and his ongoing work in film suggest an actor intent on avoiding typecasting.

With a growing family and a diverse portfolio of work across comedy, thriller, and drama genres, Calum Lill has successfully navigated the perilous transition from "soap star" to established working actor.
Calum Lill's role in *Doctors* was Chez Wilson-Needham.
Calum Lill's role in *Holby City* was Conor Henson.
Calum Lill's role in *Hollyoaks* was P.C. Carlton Smith.
Calum Lill was a Series Regular in *Coronation Street* from 2023–2024 and a Guest in 2025.
Calum Lill appeared as himself/Joel in *ITV Competition Spots* promotional adverts in 2024.
Calum Lill has a role in the full-length feature film *Derelict*.
Calum Lill played Fleshcreep in *Jack and the Beanstalk* at the Bournemouth Pavilion in 2024.
Calum Lill played Dave in *The Sociable Plover* at the Old Red Lion Theatre, London in 2025.
Calum Lill played Fleshcreep in *Jack and the Beanstalk* at the Oak Theatre, Southport in 2025.

1.title: Calum Lill
1.content:
[![Image 1: This is a good article. Click here for more information.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/9/94/Symbol_support_vote.svg/20px-Symbol_support_vote.svg.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Good_articles* "This is a good article. Click here for more information.")

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

| Calum Lill |
| --- |
| Born | 1995 or 1996 (age 29–30) |
| Occupations | Actor Car salesman |
| Years active | 2019– |
| Television | _[Coronation Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coronation\_Street "Coronation Street")_ |
| Partner | Roberta McClarron (2021–) |

**Calum Lill** (born 1995 or 1996) is a British actor. After graduating, Lill had guest roles in _[Doctors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctors\_(2000\_TV\_series) "Doctors (2000 TV series)")_ and _[Holby City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holby\_City "Holby City")_ in 2019, and he played the recurring role of [Carlton Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlton_Smith "Carlton Smith") in the soap opera _[Hollyoaks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollyoaks "Hollyoaks")_ in 2021. Lill almost quit the acting profession due to his struggle in getting acting roles and worked various jobs in between acting, including as a car salesman, which he did not like. Lill was later cast as [Joel Deering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joel_Deering "Joel Deering") in the [ITV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITV_(TV_network) "ITV (TV network)") soap opera _[Coronation Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coronation\_Street "Coronation Street")_, which he was very happy about. Lill enjoyed his experience on the soap and received praise for his portrayal of the villain and was nominated for [_Inside Soap_ Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inside_Soap_Awards "Inside Soap Awards") and a [British Soap Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Soap_Award "British Soap Award"). Lill left the role at the end of the storyline in 2024 and he then portrayed Fleshcreep in the pantomime of _[Jack and the Beanstalk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack\_and\_the\_Beanstalk "Jack and the Beanstalk")_. In 2025, Lill announced that he would be acting in _The Sociable Plover_ at the [Old Red Lion, Islington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Red_Lion,_Islington "Old Red Lion, Islington"), and that same year it was also announced that he would be briefly returning to _Coronation Street_.

Early life and career
---------------------

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Calum_Lill&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and career")]

### Early life and career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Calum_Lill&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early life and career")]

Calum Lill was born in 1995 or 1996.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Interview_2-1) Lill comes from a working-class family.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Personal-2) When he was a child, Still watch the drama _[Waterloo Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterloo\_Road\_(TV\_series) "Waterloo Road (TV series)")_, which he considered his favourite show.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Joel_1-3) He revealed, "All I wanted to do was get an acting job in _Waterloo Road_ when I was growing up".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Joel_1-3) Lill also revealed that his house was used as one of the sets during the early years of _Waterloo Road_ just as his family were moving out from it.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Joel_1-3)

Shortly after he graduated, Lill portrayed lead guest character Chez Wilson-Needham in an episode of the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC") soap opera _[Doctors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctors\_(2000\_TV\_series) "Doctors (2000 TV series)")_, which aired in 2019.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Doctors-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Doctors_2-5) Speaking of the experience, Lill said, "it was two days filming and you'd think I'd just been cast as the lead in the new [Scorsese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Scorsese "Martin Scorsese") epic".[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Personal-2) He also portrayed Conor Henson in a 2019 episode of _[Holby City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holby\_City "Holby City")_, which Lill described as "fantastic".[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Personal-2)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Personal_2-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Holby-7) The [COVID-19 lockdown in the United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_lockdown_in_the_United_Kingdom "COVID-19 lockdown in the United Kingdom") then occurred, which hindered Lill's plans.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Personal-2) Due to the television industry shutting down, Lill nearly became homeless during the pandemic.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Personal_2-6) Lill recalled to the _Me, Myself and Hopefully You..?_ podcast in 2021, "It's a hustle. That's what a lot of theatre actors struggle with. They love theatre, but it only pays enough to cover your rent while in you're in the job... You've then got to go back to waiting tables".[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Personal_2-6) In 2021, he portrayed the recurring role of [Carlton Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlton_Smith "Carlton Smith") in the soap opera _[Hollyoaks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollyoaks "Hollyoaks")_ for 12 episodes.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-8)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Personal-2)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-9)

In between acting roles, Lill had various jobs, including a stint working at Junkyard Golf Club.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Personal-2) Lill moved from London to Manchester with his girlfriend and worked alongside acting to save money for a house.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Personal-2)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Interview_2-1) Lill found this experience very difficult and was not happy in the non-acting job that he was doing, and he almost quit his acting career.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Personal-2)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Quit-10) At one point, Lill auditioned for the soap opera _[Coronation Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coronation\_Street "Coronation Street")_ but was unsuccessful, which made him upset as he wanted to be on the soap due to being working-class and Northern.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Personal-2) Lill then worked at a paella stand at festivals where he met actors [Rupert Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rupert_Hill "Rupert Hill"), the brother of the owner of the stand, and his wife [Jenny Platt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenny_Platt "Jenny Platt"), both of whom had appeared in the soap.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Personal-2)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-11) The actors reassured him that the producers of _Coronation Street_ would contact him if they liked him.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Personal-2)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Quit_2-12) Whilst auditioning for the soap, he worked as a car salesman, which he hated.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Quit-10)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Quit_2-12)

In August 2023, it was announced that Lill had joined the cast of _Coronation Street_ as [Joel Deering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joel_Deering "Joel Deering"), a solicitor who would become the new love interest for [Dee Dee Bailey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dee_Dee_Bailey "Dee Dee Bailey") ([Channique Sterling-Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channique_Sterling-Brown "Channique Sterling-Brown")).[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-14) Lill described being cast in the soap as "incredible", adding, "I've never felt anything like it. I was walking on air...especially being a working class northern lad".[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Personal-2) He added, "It was a relief that 14 or 15 years had paid off and I wouldn't have to quit. There's no shame in quitting... But to know I didn't have to was incredible".[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Personal-2) He auditioned for the role in May 2023 initially believed that he had been unsuccessful.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Interview_2-1)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Personal_2-6) When Lill's agent told him that he had received the part, he fell to his knees and cried and could not speak as he was "over the moon".[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Quit-10) The actor called getting a regular role on the soap the equivalent of getting his "letter for [Hogwarts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hogwarts "Hogwarts")".[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Interview-15) Lill revealed that _Coronation Street_ spent a lot of money on the character's outfits.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Personal-2) Lill would wake up at 5:30am to read the scripts and arrive to work for 7am and stay until about 8–9pm.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Interview_2-1)

> "When you're doing 40 pages a day then you finish and need to learn 40 pages for the next few days, it's so relentless... it's such a skill, a baptism by fire. That was the most challenging. Everyone says you'll leave a different actor then when you started, because you can't not learn and develop so fast from the sheer volume of work."

–Lill on working on _Coronation Street_ (2024)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Joel_2-16)

Joel was initially portrayed as a "good guy" but was later revealed to be a villain who was grooming and abusing girls and had tried to murder [Lauren Bolton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lauren_Bolton "Lauren Bolton") ([Cait Fitton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cait_Fitton "Cait Fitton")), who had been presumed dead for months.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Prop-17) Lill had known that Joel was going to be a villain and found out just how "bad" Joel was as he got further into auditions, and he was initially unaware of how the plot would end as it "kept changing".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Joel_1-3) Lill enjoyed portraying Joel's villainous side, as he found it more fun, but did not "camp it up" due to the storyline being a serious matter.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Interview-15) He was also uncomfortable with portraying some of the things that the character did due to it being so dark, but the crew supported him with it.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Interview-15)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Interview_3-18) Lill researched for the role by watching hours of police interviews with serial killer [Ted Bundy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Bundy "Ted Bundy") and speaking to the Maggie Oliver Foundation, a charity that supports survivors of sexual exploitation and abuse.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Interview_2-1) The actor would listen to music to get into character, ranging from sad, melancholy and drum and bass, but he noted that he could no longer listen to that music for pleasure as it would remind him of Joel.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-19) Lill joked that several viewers had recognised him in public but did not speak to him as he plays a villain, but he believed that he had created "some sort of separation" between him and the character due to being active on social media.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Joel_2-16) Lill expected to receive a negative backlash but found most of the response to be supportive.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Interview-15) He added that he only began to get noticed by viewers when Joel was revealed to be involved with Lauren.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-20) Fitton and Lill got on well together and went the "extra mile" to make their scenes believable by distancing from each other on set and being in character when they passed each other.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-21) Lill found an episode that was mostly him and Fitton to be the most challenging part of his time on the soap, but they felt "privileged" to be "trusted" with it.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Joel_2-16) In order to protect the secret from viewers that Lauren was alive, Lill would hide Fitton in the boot of his car when entering the set gates in order to sneak her into the building.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-22) Lill joked on [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram") that he struggled to act with the child actress who played Joel's daughter [Maeve Wilkinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Coronation_Street_characters_introduced_in_2024#Maeve_Wilkinson "List of Coronation Street characters introduced in 2024") as he died "of cuteness overload every take".[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-23) However, Lill also revealed that criticise himself when he would watch his scenes in episodes but added, "I worked so hard. I know that there's definitely better actors than me but I don't think anybody else could have put in as much work as I did. Because I just said, if I can give this 100% and I leave and I don't work for years, at least I know that there's no more I could have done".[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-CS_exit-24)

In July 2024, it was announced that Lill had been cast as the villain Fleshcreep in [Bournemouth Pavilion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pavilion_Theatre,_Bournemouth "Pavilion Theatre, Bournemouth")'s pantomime of _[Jack and the Beanstalk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack\_and\_the\_Beanstalk "Jack and the Beanstalk")_, which ran from December 2024 to January 2025.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-CS_exit_2-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Jack-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-27) Lill joked that he had a "streak" of playing villains.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Inside_Gossip-28) He added that he was looking forward to doing comedy.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Interview_3-18) Lill's casting in the production sparked rumours that Lill would be exiting _Coronation Street_ due to ITV usually not allowing actors to star in pantomimes while they are contracted, though it was reported that Lill had always meant to have a finite run on the soap.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-CS_exit_2-25) His departure was confirmed the following month.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-29) The character was [killed-off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Killed-off "Killed-off") in a [Whodunit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whodunit "Whodunit") mystery storyline in September 2024, and the killer was revealed to be Lauren that November in a flashback episode.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Personal-2) Lill he did not want to leave the soap as he had made some good friends there, calling it "the most incredible place to work" and "the best year" of his life.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Interview-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Joel_2-16) The ending changed several times, which kept Lill on his "toes".[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Interview_3-18) Lill had left the show in July 2024 but returned to film the flashback episode.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-CS_exit-24) Lill revealed that when he left the soap, he took several of the character's outfits, including his "smart casual stuff" which he considered "nicer" than any of his own smart outfits, with permission.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Personal-2)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-30) He also took home the "soft foam" prop of the brick that was used to kill Joel.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Personal-2) Lill's co-stars got him several leaving presents, including a St Christopher's pendant.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Interview_3-18)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-31) Lill said that leaving his colleagues would be the most difficult thing of leaving the soap as he believed that they were the "just the best in the world".[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-32)

For his role as Joel, Lill was shortlisted for "Best Villain" at the [2024 _Inside Soap_ Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inside_Soap_Awards#2024 "Inside Soap Awards"), whilst Joel being revealed as Lauren's mystery boyfriend was shortlisted for "Best Showstopper" and Lauren's disappearance was longlisted for "Best Storyline".[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-2024_award-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-2024_Shortlist-35) In 2025, Lill was longlisted for [Villain of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villain_of_the_Year "Villain of the Year") at the [British Soap Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Soap_Awards "British Soap Awards").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-BSA_longlist-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Sociable_Plover-38) He made the shortlist.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-40) Gary Brocart-Gillatt from _[Inside Soap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inside\_Soap "Inside Soap")_ wrote that he enjoyed the "camp touches" that Lill brought to his villainous character.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-41) Lill spoke to James Chase, who plays [Tom King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_King_(Emmerdale) "Thomas King (Emmerdale)") in another soap opera _[Emmerdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmerdale "Emmerdale")_, at an awards ceremony as they both related to playing villains in soap operas and received hate messages online.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Inside_Gossip-28) In November 2024, Lill appeared on _[Good Morning Britain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good\_Morning\_Britain\_(2014\_TV\_programme) "Good Morning Britain (2014 TV programme)")_, where promoted the details of an [ITV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITV_(TV_network) "ITV (TV network)") competition to viewers.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-42) In April 2025, Lill announced that he would be acting in [Tim Whitnall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Whitnall "Tim Whitnall")'s play _The Sociable Plover_ at the [Old Red Lion, Islington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Red_Lion,_Islington "Old Red Lion, Islington") from 13–24 May that year.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Sociable_Plover-38) That same month, it was reported that Lill would briefly reprise his role of Joel on _Coronation Street_ in an unknown storyline.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-CS_return-43) In October 2025, it was announced that Lill would be a celebrity judge on _Worksop's Got Talent_.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-44)

Lill has dated Roberta McClarron, who works in [public relations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_relations "Public relations") and marketing, since December 2021.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Personal-2) When he was cast on _Coronation Street_, he lived with his girlfriend and his brother, who knew about Joel turning out to be a villain.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Interview_2-1) Lill said that McClarron was very happy for him when he was cast on _Coronation Street_ as she knew how much he was struggling emotionally due to his struggles in getting acting jobs.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Personal-2)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-45) McClaron got on well with Sterling-Brown; they had a group chat with McClaron's friend called "The Girls Featuring Calum".[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Interview-15) In June 2024, the couple announced their engagement.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Personal_2-6)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-46) That September, Lill paid tribute to McClarron on [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram"), where he thanked her for supporting him and his acting career and noted that he had not seen her much during his time on _Coronation Street_ but she still supported him and did the housework so that Lill could put the soap first, with Lill writing, "I'm so grateful to have you in my life and that you agreed to marry me. Thanks for being amazing".[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-47)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Interview-15) Lill said in 2024 that he was friends with actor Tyler Dobbs, who also portrayed a villain in _Coronation Street_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Interview_2-1) In May 2024, Lill took part in the AJ Bell Great Manchester Run with other _Coronation Street_ actors to raise money for charity.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-48) Lill filmed a video of his grandmother reacting to Joel being revealed as a villain, which became popular with _Coronation Street_ viewers; Lill attributed this to viewers seeing him as "Calum the actor" rather than his character.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-49) In the first half of 2025, Lill travelled around [Southeast Asia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southeast_Asia "Southeast Asia").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calum_Lill#cite_note-Sociable_Plover-38)

2.title: Audiences enjoy first look at new Jack and the Beanstalk panto at Oak Theatre with Corrie star Calum Lill
2.description: Christmas has come to the Oak Theatre with the new state-of-the-art venue enjoying a hugely successful opening weekend for its first dazzling family pantomime. Coronation Street star Calum Lill plays the evil Fleshcreep in Jack and the Beanstalk which runs at the theatre at Scarisbrick Hall near Southport until Wednesday 24 December
2.content:
Christmas has come to the Oak Theatre with the new state-of-the-art venue enjoying a hugely successful opening weekend for its first dazzling family pantomime.

**Coronation Street star Calum Lill**plays the evil Fleshcreep in **Jack and the Beanstalk**which runs at the theatre **at Scarisbrick Hall near Southport until Wednesday 24 December 2025.**

[**Tickets for the lavish panto**](https://oaktheatreandstudios.co.uk/)**, presented by Anton Bensons Productions Ltd, are priced from £14.**

Calum, who played the Street’s bad boy Joel Deering, is joined on the Oak Theatre stage by real-life couple **Danny Childs and Suzanne Fulton** as Jack Trott and Princess Jill, **Mary Shanker** as Mary the Fairy and **Michael Lawless** as King Bling.

![Image 1: A youth stage production is presented on stage in front of a seated audience](https://standupforsouthport.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/OakTheatre-03-1-1024x562.jpg)

Jack and the Beanstalk runs at Oak Theatre at Scarisbrick Hall near Southport until Wednesday 24 December 2025. Photo by David Munn

Meanwhile due to illness, veteran panto dame David Dale has had to withdraw from the run – he has been **replaced by the very talented DG Foster**, who stepped into Dame Trott’s shoes with just a few hours’ notice to entertain audiences on opening weekend.

When Jack Trott swaps the family cow for a bag of beans, his mum isn’t best pleased. But when the beans sprout…and keep growing, they lead to the tallest of adventures in the clouds.

Can Jack outwit the wily Fleshcreep and rescue his sweetheart Princess Jill from the clutches of the giant? Or will he fee-fi-fo fumble his chance to be a hero? There’s only one way to find out.

Audiences can expect two-and-a-half hours of toe-tapping song and dance, colourful costumes, fantastic sets – encompassing the venue’s 4k digital wall, and stunning special effects all wrapped up in a hilarious laugh-a-minute script.

**Calum Lill** is best known for playing Coronation Street villain Joel Deering who met a sticky end at the heart of a dramatic whodunit which kept soap viewers on the edge of their seats. His other screen credits include PC Carlton Smith in Hollyoaks and roles in Doctors and Holby City. His stage credits include The Sociable Plover at London’s Old Red Lion. And he returns to the role of Fleshcreep after playing him last Christmas in Bournemouth.

Meanwhile when he is not causing drama on screen, he loves bringing stories to life on stage and helping other actors through his coaching company Screen Ready.

![Image 2: Man dressed in a Renaissance-style velvet outfit with floral background](https://standupforsouthport.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/OakTheatre-07-1024x682.jpg)

Calum Lil in Jack and the Beanstalk at oak Theatre. Credit David Munn

**Danny Childs is Jack Trott.** ALRA North-trained Danny is an actor and filmmaker. Previous panto appearances include Wishee Washee in Aladdin, Potty Pierre in Beauty and the Beast and Simple Simon in Jack and the Beanstalk, Buttons in Cinderella and Rafi in Rapunzel. Further stage credits include The Wish, That Sketch Show, Farmboy, The Snow Queen, and Ugly Duckling for Tutti Frutti Productions in the UK and on a US tour. Away from the stage he is co-owner of independent filmmakers Squad Four Productions.

**Suzanne Fulton plays Princess Jill and is also the show’s choreographer.** Suzanne is a Mancunian actress, choreographer and producer who trained at the Bristol Old Vic and Manchester School of Acting. Her previous panto appearances include the Fairy in Sleeping Beauty alongside Vicki Michelle, and Aladdin. Other stage credits include Silent Cicada at Liverpool Playhouse, The Wish and The Yellow Dress. Suzanne also has her own company, Parallel Productions, championing women’s voices from the north and whose productions have included Parallel Lives at the Oldham Coliseum. She recently starred in her first full-length feature film, Derelict.

![Image 3: Man in a red jumpsuit is sitting on a toilet beside a Winnie the Pooh doll, a woman is standing beside him in a long green dress and hat](https://standupforsouthport.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/OakTheatre-04-682x1024.jpg)

Jack and the Beanstalk runs at Oak Theatre at Scarisbrick Hall near Southport until Wednesday 24 December 2025. Photo by David Munn

**Mary the Fairy is played by Mary Shanker.** The Manchester-born actor, musician and singer-songwriter trained at the Liverpool Institute for Performing Arts (LIPA), and her panto credits include Cinderella last Christmas with Katie Price and Kerry Katona, Beauty and the Beast alongside Les Dennis and Jack and the Beanstalk. Her other stage credits include A Christmas Carol and Simon Says, the latter produced by the All Day Breakfast Theatre Company of which Mary is a founding member.

**Michael Lawless appears as King Bling.** Actor, singer and writer Michael, who trained at The Expressive Arts and Media Academy in Liverpool, returns to Jack and the Beanstalk after appearing in the tall tale in Dublin last Christmas. Further stage credits include The Insufferable Loneliness of Jeremy and Scuttlers, both at Manchester’s Royal Exchange.

![Image 4: Actors pose with a cow puppet on stage in front of an audience](https://standupforsouthport.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/OakTheatre-05-1024x682.jpg)

Jack and the Beanstalk runs at Oak Theatre at Scarisbrick Hall near Southport until Wednesday 24 December 2025. Photo by David Munn

**And DG Foster is Dame Trott**. Scottish-born, Newcastle-based character actor, writer and creative DG has previously played Dame Dora Crackpot in Beauty and the Beast, Sarah the Cook in Dick Whittington, the Genie in Aladdin and the Joker in the Mirror in Snow White. He also writes pantomimes. His other stage credits include Horatio in Hamlet and Bardolph in Henry V. DG is also the writer and principal narrator for YouTube channel WatchMojoUK.

The Oak Theatre is a **stunning new state-of-the-art 390-seat venue** situated in the sweeping grounds of the award-winning Scarisbrick Hall School.

![Image 5: Four female dancers in red dresses and a male dancer in a green velvet suit with a frilled scarf are performing on stage in front of a painted backdrop](https://standupforsouthport.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/OakTheatre-06-1024x682.jpg)

Jack and the Beanstalk runs at Oak Theatre at Scarisbrick Hall near Southport until Wednesday 24 December 2025. Photo by David Munn

It champions bold storytelling and boundary-pushing performances, bringing together visionary creatives and engaged audiences to shape the future of live entertainment.

The theatre has partnered with veteran panto producer**Anton Benson Productions**to present its first professional pantomime on the stage. ABP produces successful Christmas pantomimes for five other venues across the North West in addition to providing Easter pantos for more than 15 venues across the UK each spring**.**

The company has worked with many big-name stars including Les Dennis, John Thomson, Kerry Katona, Mark Labbett, Su Pollard and Basil Brush.

**Oak Theatre general manager Tom Cain said:**_“What a fantastic opening weekend we’ve enjoyed at the Oak Theatre – Jack and the Beanstalk is panto’s tallest tale, and Anton Benson Productions and their hugely talented cast, led by Calum Lill, have created a brilliant, imaginative and captivating production for our inaugural seasonal show. We’re also very grateful for DG Foster stepping in at extremely short notice – he’s an experienced panto performer, and has the audience in stitches._

_“For many children pantomime is their first taste of live theatre, so seeing the enchanted look on our young audiences’ faces, and hearing their cheers and boos, is the best feeling in the world. I’m really looking forward to sharing this fantastic production with even more festive theatregoers of all ages between now and Christmas.”_

Coronation Street star Calum Lill reveals why he nearly quit his acting career
==============================================================================

"It was a relief that 14 or 15 years had paid off and I wouldn't have to quit."

By [Harriet Mitchell](https://www.digitalspy.com/author/253238/harriet-mitchell/ "Harriet Mitchell")Published: 18 February 2024

![Image 6: Play Icon](https://www.digitalspy.com/_assets/design-tokens/fre/static/icons/play.db7c035.svg?primary=%2523ffffff)![Image 7: joel deering, toyah battersby, coronation street](https://hips.hearstapps.com/hmg-prod/images/joel-deering-toyah-battersby-coronation-street-65b231886640e.jpg?crop=1.00xw:0.834xh;0,0.0737xh)

[_Coronation Street_](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/coronation-street/) star [Calum Lill](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/coronation-street/a46830722/coronation-street-calum-lill-joel-dee-dee-wedding/) has opened up about the struggles he faced when trying to become an actor and revealed why he nearly quit.

Speaking to **Digital Spy**and other media, Lill, who stars as [Dee-Dee's duplicitous boyfriend Joel Deering](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/coronation-street/a46727525/coronation-street-spoilers-joel-deering-secret/), said he almost quit his acting career before [being cast in _Corrie_ in 2023](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/coronation-street/a44944707/coronation-street-hollyoaks-calum-lill-joel-dee-dee/).

"I was selling cars while auditioning for _Corrie_ and I hated it," he said. "I thought: 'It's been 15 years, I'm going to have to drop it, nothing's happening'.

What to Read Next
-----------------

![Image 8: joel deering, toyah battersby, coronation street](https://hips.hearstapps.com/hmg-prod/images/joel-deering-toyah-battersby-coronation-street-65b231886640e.jpg?resize=980:*)

ITV

**Related:**[**_Coronation Street_****star Calum Lill calls for Joel and Dee-Dee wedding**](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/coronation-street/a46830722/coronation-street-calum-lill-joel-dee-dee-wedding/)

"When I found out I got the part, I walked out onto the forecourt, I was between two cars. My agent said: 'Calum?' There was a silence that lasted for about ten minutes and then I heard 'You got it'. Like the absolute drama queen that I am, I just fell to my knees and was crying and sobbing, I couldn't speak. I was over the moon."

Advertisement - Continue Reading Below

After moving to Manchester with his girlfriend, Lill worked alongside acting to save for a house, describing the experience as "tough".

"Then it came along and I've never felt anything like it. I was walking on air. I felt incredible – especially being a working class northern lad. To know I've got a part in an institution like _Coronation Street_, it's the most incredible thing."

![Image 9: joel dee dee bailey coronation street](https://hips.hearstapps.com/hmg-prod/images/joel-dee-dee-bailey-coronation-street-6555f04a1ab67.jpg?crop=1.00xw:0.706xh;0,0.108xh&resize=980:*)

ITV

**Related:**[**Ellie Leach addresses****_Coronation Street_****return possibility**](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/coronation-street/a46827391/ellie-leach-coronation-street-return/)

Speaking of his girlfriend Roberta's reaction to him getting the part, Lill said: "It wasn't just happiness for me getting the job, she knew what I was going through and that I was struggling. I wasn't happy in the job that I was doing. She knew that I was putting on a brave face, but how down I was. It was a relief that 14 or 15 years had paid off and I wouldn't have to quit.

"There's no shame in quitting. So many people have to. It's one of the hardest industries to get into. But to know I didn't have to was incredible."

**_Coronation Street_****airs on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays at 8pm on ITV1 and streams on ITVX.**

Actor Calum Lill was almost ready to give up his dream job before Coronation Street

[Coronation Street's](https://www.mirror.co.uk/all-about/coronation-street)Calum Lill was on the brink of quitting acting before landing his role in the popular soap.

‌

His character Joel Deering was initially introduced as a duty solicitor assisting Lauren Bolton but soon became a permanent fixture in Weatherfield after sparking a romance with Dee-Dee Bailey. However, some residents including Alya Nazir grew suspicious of Joel and uncovered that he had a secret wife and a one year old daughter, leaving Dee-Dee devastated.

‌

Joel insisted he is divorcing his estranged wife and fighting to see his young daughter, but it remains uncertain whether Dee-Dee can forgive him for his deception. He may continue to stick around in Weatherfield if he can reconcile with girlfriend Dee-Dee, which would undoubtedly be good news for actor Calum. The star has been candid about his struggles to secure roles before his big break last year.

Article continues below

Before joining [Coronation Street](https://www.mirror.co.uk/all-about/coronation-street), Calum worked as a car salesman - a job he confessed he "hated". He admitted he thought he'd have to give up acting after facing career setbacks and struggling to find stable jobs. "I was selling cars while auditioning for Corrie and I hated it," he revealed. "I thought, 'It's been 15 years, I'm going to have to drop it, nothing's happening'."

‌

[Get More of Our News on Google Set Daily Mirror as a 'Preferred Source' to get quicker access to the news you value.](https://google.com/preferences/source?q=mirror.co.uk)

Gaining initial experience on shows like Doctors and Holby City post-graduation, Calum faced a period of no work following the onset of the lockdown. A pivotal moment came at the close of 2021 when he secured a 12-episode stint on Hollyoaks after which he worked on a paella stall at festivals alongside Coronation Street veterans [Jenny Platt](https://www.mirror.co.uk/all-about/jenny-platt) and Rupert Hill, recognised for their roles as Violet Wilson and Jamie Baldwin in the soap.

Despite an unsuccessful audition for Coronation Street at that point, Calum was buoyed up by Jenny and Rupert who assured him that if impressed, the producers would definitely get in touch with him again. In pursuit of this dream, Calum relocated to Manchester along with his girlfriend and maintained other jobs alongside his acting career in a bid to save for a house.

Eventually rewarded with the role of Joel on Corrie, Calum admitted it felt akin to "walking on air". He shared to The [Mirror](https://www.mirror.co.uk/) and other press: "It was a relief that 14 or 15 years had paid off and I wouldn't have to quit. There's no shame in quitting. So many people have to. It's one of the hardest industries to get into. But to know I didn't have to was incredible."

Article continues below

His girlfriend was equally overjoyed when he landed the role on Coronation Street after a two-year dry spell. "My girlfriend Roberta is incredible," said Calum. "When I told her I got the role, she was screaming and crying. I was crying too. She knew I'd been putting on a brave face and it was a huge relief that 15 years of hard work paid off."

Actor Calum Lill has officially bowed out of the ITV soap after 14 months of playing the twisted solicitor.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Coronation Street star Calum Lill has shared some of the secrets of filming his final scenes as Joel Deering. The actor has officially bowed out of the ITV soap after 14 months of playing the twisted solicitor.

As fans know, Joel arrived onto the cobbles in September 2023 as a charming solicitor who Dee-Dee Bailey soon fell head over heels in love with. But under his smooth exterior Joel was hiding a dark secret - a penchant for younger, underprivileged girls.

When Lauren [Bolton](https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/all-about/bolton) went missing in February of this year, it was later revealed that Joel was responsible, having abused his position as her duty solicitor, to subject her to a torrent of both physical and verbal abuse which led to her fleeing the street fearing for her life, and ended up fleeing the street following his vicious attack.

**READ MORE: [Coronation Street's Peter Ash supported by co-stars as he confirms huge acting move after tragic soap exit](https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/news/showbiz-news/coronation-streets-peter-ash-supported-30376311)**

**READ MORE: [Read more of our Coronation Street stories here](https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/all-about/coronation-street)**

But after the truth was starting to come out, thanks to his fiancée Dee-Dee Bailey and DS Lisa Swian, Joel was declared missing after he failed to show his face in court. In the scenes aired at the end of September, a warrant was issued for Joel's arrest as he was seemingly set to face his comeuppance for his twisted crimes, which included grooming Lauren Bolton.

After transferring money to Lauren, how the mother of his son Frankie and his ex-wife Emily, and leaving an emotional voicemail for his former fiancée Dee-Dee Bailey, Joel's car was found abandoned and it was believed Joel may have ended up taking his own life.

The police carried on investigating and it wasn't long before the case became a murder investigation after Joel's body was found floating down a river. However, it was confirmed he'd been killed with a heavy weapon before entering the water and several people were been put in the frame for his murder.

But on Friday night (November 15), Joel's murderer was revealed in a stunning episode which featured a series of flashbacks from the night of Joel’s murder, interspersed with DC Kit Green's police interviews, bringing what really happened on September 27th.

It was an eventful night for Joel, after Ronnie and Ed Bailey went after him with a crowbar, he was attacked by scorned ex Dee-Dee, threatened by Kit and pushed into the river by Max. But not before Lauren had delivered the killer blow amidst the train track confrontation.

The final scenes mean Calum's time as Joel has officially come to an end and he's revealed to the Manchester Evening News just what it was like to film them. The final episode was months in the planning with all the flashback scenes, which were filmed about 10 weeks ago and shot out of order like a jigsaw.

"I kind of left and came back," he told us. "I finished in July really, then just came back to film my final episode and it was nice to come back and see everyone. But when I came back, it was like we were filming a movie. One of the scenes, we spent 12 hours shooting. We had all these different cameras and green screens and special effects. I've never experienced anything like that before so it was incredible."I've played him nice, I've played him funny, I've played him boring, I've played him horrific, then I've managed to do the soap stuff on location and also on this movie set. Where we were filming, it was Peaky Blinders movie, House of Guinness, Talamasca, these big Hollywood films and then us. It was incredible to have gotten that opportunity so yeah it was amazing, I'm looking forward to seeing it, I can't wait."

A volume wall was used to film the scenes, so the cast weren't really on a railway bridge but was inside a Greater Manchester studio. "It was in Gorton, this massive huge black room," Calum shared. "The ceiling was probably about 70 feet high. It's just this massive semi-circle of screens and then you're set in the middle, so we've got this long railway bridge that we've built and that's on a table that turns.

"So instead of the camera moving, the camera stays where it is, the train track moves and the whole background is synced with the cameras. When the camera moves, the background moves as if the camera's moving in the real place. They go out to the real bridge, take 360 views of the whole place and then wire the camera up so the background scenes change. It's really hard \[to explain\], when you see it hopefully it will explain. It looks like the cameras are moving all around the bridge but the cameras never move. It's crazy but really cool."

But it was when the soap star was asked if he'd taken anything of Joel's with him a memento of his time playing the character when Calum revealed more details. "I've got the murder weapon at home," he said. "It's like a brick that would have been part of the bridge, so I've got the foam soft version. Not soft enough to be hit as hard as I was getting hit in the face repeatedly by Cait but softer than a brick nonetheless.

"Duncan the director was like: 'We can tell that you're being too gentle with him, go on, he's a big lad'. I was like: 'Cait, we've worked on this, this is the final, we've worked together for so long, sell this, this is the last bit, go for it'. She did! Luckily the next day of filming was just being dead on the train track, which was good because I needed a lie down! That's what I did for the next 12 hours."

Jack and the Beanstalk runs at Oak Theatre at Scarisbrick Hall near Southport from Saturday 13th December  Wednesday 24th December 2025

SHARE

[](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=First+look+at+cast+set+to+entertain+families+at+giant+new+Jack+and+the+Beanstalk+pantomime&url=https%3A%2F%2Fstandupforsouthport.com%2Ffirst-look-at-cast-set-to-entertain-families-at-giant-new-jack-and-the-beanstalk-pantomime%2F&via=andrewbrownedit)[](mailto:?subject=First%20look%20at%20cast%20set%20to%20entertain%20families%20at%20giant%20new%20Jack%20and%20the%20Beanstalk%20pantomime%20|%20Stand%20Up%20For%20Southport&body=I%20found%20this%20article%20interesting%20and%20thought%20of%20sharing%20it%20with%20you.%20Check%20it%20out:%0A%0Ahttps%3A%2F%2Fstandupforsouthport.com%2Ffirst-look-at-cast-set-to-entertain-families-at-giant-new-jack-and-the-beanstalk-pantomime%2F)[](https://standupforsouthport.com/first-look-at-cast-set-to-entertain-families-at-giant-new-jack-and-the-beanstalk-pantomime/#)[](javascript:if(window.print)window.print())[](https://standupforsouthport.com/first-look-at-cast-set-to-entertain-families-at-giant-new-jack-and-the-beanstalk-pantomime/#)

Christmas comes to the Oak Theatre this December – and ahead of that can be revealed the first look at the talented cast who are set to dazzle family audiences at the new state-of-the-art venue.

**Coronation Street star Calum Lill**plays the evil Fleshcreep in **Jack and the Beanstalk**which runs at the theatre **at Scarisbrick Hall near Southport from Saturday 13th December – Wednesday 24th December 2025.**

**Tickets are on sale now priced from £14.**

The lavish panto is presented by Anton Benson Productions Ltd.

Calum, who played the Street’s bad boy Joel Deering, will be joined on the Oak Theatre stage by legendary **pantomime dame David Dale** who appears as Dame Trott, real-life couple **Danny Childs and Suzanne Fulton** as Jack Trott and Princess Jill, **Mary Shanker** as Mary the Fairy and **Michael Lawless** as King Bling.

When Jack Trott swaps the family cow for a bag of beans, his mum isn’t best pleased. But when the beans sprout…and keep growing, they lead to the tallest of adventures in the clouds.

Can Jack outwit the wily Fleshcreep and rescue his sweetheart Princess Jill from the clutches of the giant? Or will he fee-fi-fo fumble his chance to be a hero? There’s only one way to find out.

Audiences can expect two-and-a-half hours of toe-tapping song and dance, colourful costumes, fantastic sets – encompassing the venue’s 4k digital wall, and stunning special effects all wrapped up in a hilarious laugh-a-minute script.

**Calum Lill** is best known for playing Coronation Street villain Joel Deering who met a sticky end at the heart of a dramatic whodunit which kept soap viewers on the edge of their seats. His other screen credits include PC Carlton Smith in Hollyoaks and roles in Doctors and Holby City. His stage credits include The Sociable Plover at London’s Old Red Lion. And he returns to the role of Fleshcreep after playing him last Christmas in Bournemouth.

![Image 10: A woman in costume with fairy wings stands next to a man in a green velvet suit and matching top hat, both with displeased expressions, in front of a sign reading OAK](https://standupforsouthport.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/OakTheatre-03.jpg)

Jack and the Beanstalk runs at Oak Theatre at Scarisbrick Hall near Southport from Saturday 13th December  Wednesday 24th December 2025. Calum Lil as Fleshcreep

Meanwhile when he is not causing drama on screen, he loves bringing stories to life on stage and helping other actors through his coaching company Screen Ready.

**David Dale plays Dame Trott and also directs.** Panto royalty David has worked with all the major pantomime production companies and has appeared in more than 25 seasonal shows as well as directing six pantos. His highlights include pantomimes at the London Palladium and Birmingham Hippodrome among many other leading venues. In 2024 he was nominated for a prestigious UK Pantomime Award alongside fellow ‘Ugly Sister’ James Holmes for their double act in Cinderella at the Buxton Opera House.

His other stage credits over a four-decade career include The Rocky Horror Show and Women Behind Bars in the West End. His screen credits include EastEnders, Father Ted (playing a nun) and The Sins.

**Danny Childs is Jack Trott.** ALRA North-trained Danny is an actor and filmmaker. Previous panto appearances include Wishee Washee in Aladdin, Potty Pierre in Beauty and the Beast and Simple Simon in Jack and the Beanstalk, Buttons in Cinderella and Rafi in Rapunzel. Further stage credits include The Wish, That Sketch Show, Farmboy, The Snow Queen, and Ugly Duckling for Tutti Frutti Productions in the UK and on a US tour. Away from the stage he is co-owner of independent filmmakers Squad Four Productions.

**Suzanne Fulton plays Princess Jill and is also the show’s choreographer.** Suzanne is a Mancunian actress, choreographer and producer who trained at the Bristol Old Vic and Manchester School of Acting. Her previous panto appearances include the Fairy in Sleeping Beauty alongside Vicki Michelle, and Aladdin. Other stage credits include Silent Cicada at Liverpool Playhouse, The Wish and The Yellow Dress. Suzanne also has her own company, Parallel Productions, championing women’s voices from the north and whose productions have included Parallel Lives at the Oldham Coliseum. She recently starred in her first full-length feature film, Derelict.

![Image 11: Group of six actors in pantomime costume pose for the camera](https://standupforsouthport.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/OakTheatre-02-1024x683.jpg)

Jack and the Beanstalk runs at Oak Theatre at Scarisbrick Hall near Southport from Saturday 13th December  Wednesday 24th December 2025.

**Mary the Fairy is played by Mary Shanker.** The Manchester-born actor, musician and singer-songwriter trained at the Liverpool Institute for Performing Arts (LIPA), and her panto credits include Cinderella last Christmas with Katie Price and Kerry Katona, Beauty and the Beast alongside Les Dennis and Jack and the Beanstalk. Her other stage credits include A Christmas Carol and Simon Says, the latter produced by the All Day Breakfast Theatre Company of which Mary is a founding member.

**And Michael Lawless appears as King Bling.** Actor, singer and writer Michael, who trained at The Expressive Arts and Media Academy in Liverpool, returns to Jack and the Beanstalk after appearing in the tall tale in Dublin last Christmas. Further stage credits include The Insufferable Loneliness of Jeremy and Scuttlers, both at Manchester’s Royal Exchange.

The Oak Theatre is a **stunning new state-of-the-art 390-seat venue** situated in the sweeping grounds of the award-winning Scarisbrick Hall School.

![Image 12: Six people in costume in front of the Oak Theatre logo](https://standupforsouthport.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/OakTheatre-04-1024x683.jpg)

Jack and the Beanstalk runs at Oak Theatre at Scarisbrick Hall near Southport from Saturday 13th December  Wednesday 24th December 2025.

It champions bold storytelling and boundary-pushing performances, bringing together visionary creatives and engaged audiences to shape the future of live entertainment.

The theatre has partnered with veteran panto producer**Anton Benson Productions**to present its first professional pantomime on the stage. ABP produces successful Christmas pantomimes for five other venues across the North West in addition to providing Easter pantos for more than 15 venues across the UK each spring**.**

The company has worked with many big-name stars including Les Dennis, John Thomson, Kerry Katona, Mark Labbett, Su Pollard and Basil Brush.

**Oak Theatre general manager Tom Cain said:**_“Excitement is really building here at the Oak Theatre with just a month to go before we welcome the first audiences to our first spectacular pantomime. Seeing our fabulous, talented cast in full costume has really got us in the Christmas spirit, and I can’t wait for opening night – I know theatregoers of all ages are going to be in for a real treat.”_

**Schools’ performances will take place during the day from 15 – 19 December**. Contact enquiries@oaktheatre.co.uk
